Monaco.text: It stopped collecting income tax from its residents in 1869, an indulgence paid for by its casino at Monte Carlo.
Monaco.evidence: In 1869, the principality stopped collecting income tax from its residents, an indulgence the Grimaldi family could afford to entertain thanks solely to the extraordinary success of the casino.

San Marino.text: Founded, it says, in AD 301, it claims to be the oldest country still standing and the oldest constitutional republic.
San Marino.evidence: San Marino claims to have been founded in AD 301 and to be the oldest extant sovereign state, and the oldest constitutional republic.

Japan.text: The longest-lived country of over 50,000 people: in the UN's table, only Hong Kong, a Chinese territory, tops it.
Japan.evidence: UN table (2023): Hong Kong 85.51, Japan 84.71, South Korea 84.33. "Only countries with populations over 50,000 are listed. Due to this criterion, the table does not include such countries as Monaco (LE 86.37 years, population 39,000), San Marino (LE 85.71 years, population 34,000)"

South Korea.text: As recently as 2008 it ranked only 34th in the world for life expectancy.
South Korea.evidence: South Korea has experienced a dramatic increase in life expectancy, from 79.10 years in 2008 (which was 34th in the world), to 83.53 years in 2024

Andorra.text: Its two heads of state are a Spanish bishop and the president of France.
Andorra.evidence: It is currently headed by two co-princes: the Bishop of Urgell in Catalonia, Spain, and the president of France.

Switzerland.text: The Swiss live 3.6 years longer than the average in the OECD's rich countries.
Switzerland.evidence: The country records a life expectancy of 83.9 years, which is 3.6 years higher than the OECD average.

Australia.text: Since 1981 a singing cartoon seagull, Sid, has told Australians to "Slip, Slop, Slap" against skin cancer.
Australia.evidence: an anthropomorphic mascot named Sid the Seagull would sing and dance to the phrase. The campaign, originally funded by public donations, was launched by Cancer Council Victoria in 1981 to combat high rates of skin cancer in Australia

Singapore.text: A 2019 study gave it the longest life expectancy of any country: 84.8 years.
Singapore.evidence: In 2019, Singaporeans had the longest life expectancy of any country at 84.8 years.

Italy.text: Mountain villages in Sardinia were the first "blue zone", named for the blue pen scientists used to mark long-lived places on a map.
Italy.evidence: who "used a blue pen on a map to mark the villages with long-lived population." ... In the original study of centenarians living in 14 mountain villages of Sardinia (the first proposed blue zone)

Spain.text: COVID-19 cut its life expectancy by more than a year in 2020.
Spain.evidence: In January 2020, the COVID-19 virus was confirmed to have spread to Spain, causing life expectancy to drop by more than a year.
